messages:
Maria H.: Hey team — kicking off a short thread to align Q3 runtime bets. We need a concrete proposal for what we ship in the next quarter (kernels, quant, KV cache ops, canaries) and hard launch criteria. TL;DR: prioritize low-latency path for short prompts + safe cost wins for embeddings workloads.
Alex T.: Agree. can we define top 3 customer-driven asks we bake into the roadmap?
Jamie (sales): From the field: AcmeHealth needs p95 < 120ms for short chat queries (<=64 tokens), and BetaRetail wants 2x throughput on embeddings at same cost. Both willing to sign dedicated if SLA met.
Kevin L.: For p95 target we need fused-attn + better KV reuse on chat sessions. Also need int8 kernels for cost. Are we comfortable shipping int8 in Q3 or should that be a Q4 canary?
Sophie R.: I'd prefer int8 as a gated canary. We don't have QA coverage for hallucination regressions with quantized runs. Proposal: limited canary to internal traffic + 5% of customer traffic for 2 weeks, with evals and rollback hooks.
Maria H.: Sounds reasonable. Let's make launch criteria explicit: 1) p95 latency (<=64 tokens) < 120ms on our representative hw, 2) throughput per-GPU >= 800 toks/s for long-runner embedding workload, 3) model quality regression delta < 0.5% on core eval set, 4) fallback policy in place (int8 -> fp16) with automagic routing. Thoughts?
Alex T.: Those metrics look good. For (1) we need a baseline harness. I'll create a bench job that runs these profiles daily.
Kevin L.: We'll need kernel priority list: 1) fused-attn + kv-prefetch, 2) flash-attn fallback, 3) int8 matmul kernels. Also add a simple metric: cache hit ratio target >= 70% for sessionized workloads.
Maria H.: Add that as #5. Also include cost delta target: int8 should reduce token cost by >= 30% or it's not worth the rollout complexity.
Jamie (sales): Prioritize AcmeHealth compatibility: TLS+KMS + private deployment option. They need predictable p95 in their VPC.
Sophie R.: Ops concern: KV cache eviction policy tuning will impact long-tail latency. We should run an A/B with LFU vs TTL policies. Small experiment, 50/50 split per customer segment.
Kevin L.: Agreed. Plan for experiments: 
```
# rollout config
- canary: 5% traffic
- phase1: internal + infra tests (1 week)
- phase2: 5% external (2 weeks)
- phase3: 25% + monitor (1 week)
- full: 100% if all gates pass
```
Alex T.: For gating we need automated checks: p95 latency, token-cost delta, eval-regressions, and error-rate spike < 0.2%. I'll wire these into the canary pipeline.
Maria H.: Ownership: Kevin (kernels + quant), Sophie (KV cache + canary gating), Alex (bench + observability), Jamie (customer rollouts / sales coordination).
Jamie (sales): I'll line up AcmeHealth for a dedicated test window in mid-Q3 so we can validate VPC perf.
Sophie R.: One more operational ask: add a fallback route in router config so when int8 fails quality gate we automatically flip traffic to fp16 variant. Example rule: `if quality_score_drop > 0.5% then route -> model/fp16/vX`.
Kevin L.: We also need a regression suite focused on top-10 prompts from production. I'll extract the prompt corpus and create diffs for quantized runs.
Alex T.: Timeline proposal: Week 1-2: bench harness + kernel perf spikes; Week 3-5: implement int8 canary + KV policy AB; Week 6: customer validation with AcmeHealth; Week 7: decision gate. OKRs to link: reduce hosted token-cost by 20% for embeddings, p95 <= 120ms for short-chat.
Maria H.: That timeline is tight but workable. Can each owner drop a short checklist into the roadmap doc by EOD Friday? I'll synthesize for planning review Monday.
Jamie (sales): +1. I'll confirm AcmeHealth availability.
infra-bot: deployment scheduled: canary-cluster-09 -> 2023-07-22T04:00Z (automated message).
Sophie R.: Quick note: let's capture expected risk list in the doc: kernel stability, quant quality drift, KV eviction regressions, rollout automation gaps. We'll add mitigation for each.
Kevin L.: I'll add improved canary observability: per-variant token-level diffs and per-user latency heatmaps.
Maria H.: Great. If no objections I'll finalize these as the Q3 runtime pillars and push to planning board. :thumbsup:
Alex T.: No objections from infra side. :eyes:
Jamie (sales): Ship it.
Sophie R.: Thanks — will add AB test spec.
